title: Bing Crosby's influence on singers of the 1930s
summary: Crouch asks about Crosby's influence on singers like Sy Oliver, and Crawford says Crosby influenced Sinatra and others.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Well, I was listening to something of -- one of the Lunceford numbers, and Sy Oliver was singing.
Well, there was something I wanted to ask you, because I had heard -- well, it sounds to me -- now, see, I may have this maybe absolutely wrong --
Then ask me, I'll tell you who he was.
But, it's like -- it sounds to me sometimes as though Bing Crosby had an effect on the way guys sang in the '30s.

Well, certainly. He had an effect on Sinatra, all of them. He was before Sinatra. But as music went, the style of playing and the style of sounds like years ago, you had the honky tonk travelling music. And then it went into swing and then it went into -- I mean, it went into Dixieland, and then from Dixieland it went into swing. And then it went into bebop. And it's just changed.
Like, you were talking about singers. Now, I -- Bing Crosby had to have some kind of influence on Sinatra.
Well, do you think he had any influence on singers like Benny Carter and Sy Oliver and any of the black singers?
Yes, well, certainly, because he came along first.
